_comment: Baked-in disruptions, each swapping the active risk event over ONE shared shipment pool. Each is chosen to force a DIFFERENT decision type - if two produced the same decision, one would be redundant. Events use the same schema as live ones, so they flow through the real pipeline.
_timestamps: published_offset_minutes is relative to load, so a scenario always reads as fresh.
_honesty: Every scenario is SCRIPTED and labelled so on screen. The live news pull runs alongside as its own genuinely live element.

scenarios.name: Hamburg port strike
scenarios.summary: A full-day walkout closes Hamburg's container terminals. Shipments with slack move to Rotterdam; the tight cold-chain one is better off waiting.
scenarios.expected: SHP-001 and SHP-005 reroute · SHP-002 holds · the rest unaffected

events.title: Warning strike at Port of Hamburg - union calls full-day walkout
events.title_original: Warnstreik im Hamburger Hafen — ver.di ruft zu ganztägigem Ausstand auf
events.summary: The service union ver.di has called a full-day warning strike across container terminals at the Port of Hamburg in the current collective bargaining round. Terminal handling, gate operations and rail shunting are expected to stop for the duration of the walkout, with vessel backlogs clearing over the following days.
events.reasoning: Union-called full-day walkout at all Hamburg container terminals; handling and gate operations stop, so any box discharging at HAM is exposed. Picked up from a German-language regional feed roughly a day before the English wires carried it.

scenarios.name: Red Sea closure
scenarios.summary: Attacks on shipping close the Bab-el-Mandeb approach, taking the Suez route with it. Almost the whole board routes that way, so every shipment has to weigh the Cape of Good Hope against waiting.
scenarios.decision_type: Forced long-haul reroute under cost and time pressure
scenarios.expected: The whole board lights up · the ones with slack take the Cape · the tight ones hold

events.title: Carriers suspend Bab-el-Mandeb transits after further attacks on merchant shipping
events.title_original: شركات الشحن توقف عبور باب المندب بعد هجمات جديدة على السفن التجارية
events.summary: Major container lines have suspended southern Red Sea transits following further attacks on merchant vessels. Services are being re-routed around the Cape of Good Hope, adding roughly ten to fourteen days to Asia-Europe strings and tightening capacity across the trade.
events.detected_first_from: Arabic-language RSS (Al Jazeera), ahead of the English maritime wires
events.reasoning: Lines are suspending Bab-el-Mandeb transits outright rather than convoying, so anything routed through Suez is re-timed around Africa. This hits every Asia-Europe string on the board at once.

events.title: Suez Canal transit bookings fall sharply as lines divert around Africa
events.summary: Canal authority transit bookings have dropped as carriers route Asia-Europe services around the Cape, leaving Suez schedules unreliable for the coming weeks.
events.reasoning: Suez schedules are unreliable while the southern approach is being avoided, so a Suez routing cannot be relied on even where the canal itself is open.

scenarios.name: Rhine low water
scenarios.summary: Sustained low water at Kaub cuts barge payloads on the Rhine. The sea leg is untouched - the cargo reaches Rotterdam fine. The problem is the barge run upcountry.
scenarios.decision_type: Inland leg re-mode: barge to rail/road, not a port change
scenarios.expected: SHP-006 switches mode · everything else stays green

events.title: Rhine low water at Kaub cuts barge payloads to a fraction of capacity
events.title_original: Niedrigwasser am Rhein: Pegel Kaub zwingt Binnenschiffe zu drastischen Teilladungen
events.summary: The reference gauge at Kaub has fallen below the level at which Rhine barges can load normally, forcing operators to sail part-loaded. Sustained dry weather upstream means levels are expected to stay low, and freight is being shifted to rail and road where capacity allows.
events.source: tagesschau (German-language RSS) corroborated by the PEGELONLINE Kaub gauge
events.detected_first_from: German-language RSS plus the Kaub water-level gauge
events.reasoning: Kaub below the loading threshold means barges sail part-laden and slots requeue, so any Rhine barge leg is delayed even though the sea leg and the discharge port are working normally.

scenarios.name: Southern France wildfire
scenarios._enabled_note: Authored and ready, switched off by default. Its decision type overlaps the Rhine scenario's inland theme, which is why it is the fourth rather than one of the core three.
scenarios.summary: Wildfire across the Rhone corridor closes road and rail inland of Fos-sur-Mer. The port keeps working; the route to Lyon does not.
scenarios.decision_type: Regional inland corridor blocked - reroute the land leg or wait
scenarios.expected: SHP-007 is actioned · everything else unaffected

events.title: Wildfire closes A7 motorway and the Rhone rail corridor north of Fos-sur-Mer
events.title_original: Incendie: l'A7 et la ligne ferroviaire de la vallée du Rhône coupées au nord de Fos-sur-Mer
events.summary: A fast-moving wildfire has closed the A7 motorway and the parallel rail freight corridor north of Fos-sur-Mer. The port continues to work cargo, but inland movement towards Lyon is suspended while firefighting continues.
events.reasoning: The discharge port is working normally; the exposure is the land corridor to Lyon, so the decision is about the inland leg rather than the port.

_languages: Each event carries a language_trail: which languages carried the story, in what order, and how far behind the English wires were. The lag is computed from the trail rather than asserted separately.
